article_notes: Prospective OVAH ICU study of B. rossi (PCR/RLB): 75 enrolled, 69 met criteria, 1 euthanased for other reasons excluded, leaving 11 non-survivors and 57 survivors. Admission samples taken before any therapy. Only CRP was studied. Age and sex were model covariates; their own associations with outcome are not reported.

severity_definitions.label: non-survivors vs survivors
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs admitted to the OVAH ICU with PCR/RLB-confirmed B. rossi; outcome survived to discharge or died. Dogs euthanased for reasons other than poor prognosis were excluded, so euthanasia for poor prognosis is taken as counted with deaths.
severity_definitions.quote: Outcome was recorded as the patient survived and was discharged or died.

severity_definitions.label: length of ICU stay (days hospitalised) in survivors
severity_definitions.definition: Number of days of hospitalisation in the ICU among survivors (continuous).
severity_definitions.quote: Among survivors, multiple regression analysis was used to examine the relationship between CRP concentration at admission and length of stay in ICU, adjusting for age and sex.

associations.statistic: mean ± SD 122.1 ± 64.6 (non-survivors) vs 107.5 ± 49.5 (survivors); exact logistic regression adjusted for age and sex
associations.note: Unit printed as 'mg/' (litre symbol lost in conversion). Direction from the group means; no odds ratio printed.
associations.quote: Using exact logistic regression, adjusting for age and sex, there was no statistically significant association between admission CRP concentration and survival ( P = 0.53).

associations.statistic: survival 100 % (9/9) with CRP < 60 vs 81.4 % (48/59) with CRP >= 60; Fisher's exact test
associations.note: Cut-off chosen post hoc as the value below which all dogs survived; no non-survivor had CRP < 63.2. Values are survival by CRP group, not CRP by outcome group, so severe_value/comparison_value are left null.
associations.quote: the survival rate for dogs with an admission CRP concentration <60 mg/ was 100 % (9/9) and those dogs with an admission CRP concentration ≥ 60 mg/ was 81.4 % (48/59). However, these 2 proportions did not differ significantly using a Fisher’s exact test ( P = 0.34).

associations.statistic: multiple regression of length of ICU stay on admission CRP, adjusted for age and sex
associations.note: Fig. 2 legend gives P = 0.64 for the same analysis; both non-significant, so significant = no. Authors note an apparent linear trend in the box plot.
associations.quote: the multiple regression analysis failed to show a significant relationship between these 2 variables, adjusting for age and sex ( P = 0.65)

associations.statistic: multiple linear regression of days hospitalised on magnitude of CRP change in first 24 h, adjusted for age and sex
associations.note: Methods state adjustment for age and sex. The 24-h sample was taken after treatment had started.
associations.marker_as_reported: change in serum CRP over the first 24 h
associations.quote: there was no significant association between the magnitude of change in CRP concentration over the 1st 24 hours from admission and the number of days of hospitalisation ( P = 0.34)

associations.statistic: median days hospitalised 3 (range 2–4; n = 9) with CRP < 60 vs 2 (range 1–6; n = 48) with CRP >= 60; Wilcoxon rank-sum
associations.note: Groups defined by the marker; the outcome (days hospitalised) is compared. Median stay was longer in the low-CRP group, hence negative_association (not significant).
associations.quote: admission CRP concentration <60 mg/ (3 days, range 2–4 days; n = 9) compared with those survivors with an admission CRP concentration ≥ 60 mg/ (2 days, range 1–6 days; n = 48), using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test ( P = 0.25)
